text.p: Sara Netanyahu, 37-year-old wife of Israel's prime minister, was back in the tabloids on Wednesday after it emerged that her ex-husband plans to publish a book about their six-year marriage that ended in 1987.
"The book is certainly not going to be an album of compliments," Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu's lawyer, David Shimron, told Israel Radio, acknowledging he had not seen the manuscript.

Three months ago Mrs Netanyahu -- propelled into the media spotlight by the new prime minister -- felt the glare of some unwanted publicity when her nanny quit in a huff saying the first lady was a harsh taskmaster with a sharp temper.
The nanny bolted after an argument over burnt soup. This time, the hot issue is secrets -- state and private.

Israel's Channel Two television began the latest chapter of what newspapers coined "The Life of Sara" with a report that former husband Doron Neuberger would "tell all" because he was upset by a photo of her looking at a classified state document.

"The photograph shows Mrs Netanyahu sitting next to (the prime minister) looking at their itinerary for a trip to Washington. The time they eat lunch and take the kids to the zoo is not exactly a state secret," he said.
Shimron said he had met once with Neuberger's lawyer to complain the book would be an invasion of privacy.
"It's a very ugly thing," he said, adding he might advise Mrs Netanyahu to take legal action "if the book contains libel".
No one was commenting on exactly what marital tidbits might be on offer.
"Even if you are married to the prime minister, that doesn't give somebody the right to expose what you did or said years ago," Shimron said.
Israeli Army Radio reported that Neuberger, who lives on a kibbutz, or collective farm, was negotiating publication rights with Israeli tabloids.

Mrs Netanyahu has been fairer game for the Israeli press than the wives of previous leaders because of her current husband's penchant for taking her on state trips and holding her hand in public in the style of U.S. presidential spouses.

But Mrs Netanyahu, though frequently at the prime minister's side, has been a silent partner -- letting her husband do all the talking. Sara is the third wife of the twice-divorced Netanyahu, who in 1993 admitted cheating on her. They have two sons, aged four and one.

Asked how the first lady felt about the book, Shimron replied: "It certainly is not pleasant. Who would be happy to hear that this kind of a book is going to be published about you? But she is a very strong woman."
